Derived from `src/cocos/dragon-bones/DragonBonesAtlasAsset.ts`, `src/cocos/dragon-bones/DragonBonesAsset.ts`, `src/cocos/dragon-bones/ArmatureDisplay.ts`, `src/cocos/dragon-bones/CCFactory.ts`, `src/cocos/dragon-bones/CCTextureData.ts`, `src/cocos/dragon-bones/CCSlot.ts`, `src/cocos/dragon-bones/index.ts`, `src/node_modules/@cocos/dragonbones-js/out/dragonBones.js`, `docs/notes/dragonbones-notes.md`, `examples/dragonbones-basic/main.js`, `build/cocosair.module.js` (as of 2026-10-10).

# What it does

DragonBones is the fully runnable skeletal 2D subsystem of the default bundle. An `ArmatureDisplay`
component plays an armature built from two JSON strings (skeleton plus atlas) and one `Texture2D`,
skinning on the vendored upstream `@cocos/dragonbones-js` algorithm. Unlike Spine it needs no wasm
backend: it is pure TypeScript against a real parser, so an armature that is wired correctly draws
on the first frame. The bundle export block of `build/cocosair.module.js` (currently `:161574`)
carries `index$1 as dragonBones`, and the component classes resolve through that namespace.

# Construction chain (three objects and one key)

1. `new DragonBonesAtlasAsset()` takes no name argument (`src/cocos/dragon-bones/DragonBonesAtlasAsset.ts:44`). Its `atlasJson` setter runs `JSON.parse` (`:53-59`, parse at `:59`), so hand it the raw atlas text, not a `JsonAsset`. `texture` wants a `Texture2D` (`:86-90`).
2. `new DragonBonesAsset(name)` (`src/cocos/dragon-bones/DragonBonesAsset.ts:67-70`) takes its skeleton through the `dragonBonesJson` text setter (`:58`).
3. `CCFactory.getInstance()` (`src/cocos/dragon-bones/CCFactory.ts:65`) is the shared parser and builder used by both assets (`:129`, `:136`).
4. `asset.init(factory, atlasUuid)` returns the armature key `uuid#atlasUUID` (`src/cocos/dragon-bones/DragonBonesAsset.ts:99-128`). When the asset is built manually, the uuid falls back to the parsed data name (`src/cocos/dragon-bones/DragonBonesAtlasAsset.ts:126`).

# Contracts

- The `ArmatureDisplay` setters are the refresh mechanism, so order matters. `dragonAsset` (`src/cocos/dragon-bones/ArmatureDisplay.ts:203-216`) and `dragonAtlasAsset` (`:226-231`) each rebuild; assign both assets before setting `armatureName` (`:239-245`), which also rebuilds.
- Cache mode defaults to `REALTIME` (`src/cocos/dragon-bones/ArmatureDisplay.ts:513`) and `_defaultCacheMode` silently downgrades to it whenever caching is unavailable (`:352-363`); a cached-mode request is not a guarantee you get cached skinning.
- `armature` is a METHOD, not a field (`src/cocos/dragon-bones/ArmatureDisplay.ts:1469`); reading it as a property gives a function, not the live armature.
- `playAnimation(name, playTimes)` treats `0` as play-once semantics, so looping requires `-1` (`src/cocos/dragon-bones/ArmatureDisplay.ts:1269`, `docs/notes/dragonbones-notes.md:68`).
- `premultipliedAlpha` defaults to `false` (`src/cocos/dragon-bones/ArmatureDisplay.ts:412`), the opposite of `sp.Skeleton`, so a shared material copied between the two subsystems is wrong on one side.
- Events go through `addEventListener` on the display (`src/cocos/dragon-bones/ArmatureDisplay.ts:1428`) with DragonBones event names, not the Cocos node emitter.

# The vendored dragonbones-js boundary

`src/cocos/dragon-bones/index.ts:105` re-exports all of `@cocos/dragonbones-js`, shipped as
`src/node_modules/@cocos/dragonbones-js/out/dragonBones.js` (15174 lines) and regenerated by
`npm run vendor:npm`. Because that file is the upstream algorithm, `AnimationCacheMode`, `Slot`,
`Armature` and the texture-data classes are named exactly as upstream - do not rename them to a
Cocos-style spelling. The AIR-side bridges are `CCTextureAtlasData` and `CCTextureData`, which
carry a `SpriteFrame` per region (`src/cocos/dragon-bones/CCTextureData.ts:37`, `:105`), and
`CCSlot`, which bakes its vertices from those regions (`src/cocos/dragon-bones/CCSlot.ts:38`,
`:229-238`).

# Gotchas

- The atlas asset will not accept a texture until an `ImageAsset` is wrapped into a `Texture2D`; `examples/dragonbones-basic/main.js:239-252` shows the required wrap before `atlasAsset.texture` is set.
- `atlasJson` and `dragonBonesJson` are text setters that parse (`src/cocos/dragon-bones/DragonBonesAtlasAsset.ts:53-59`, `src/cocos/dragon-bones/DragonBonesAsset.ts:58`); passing a loaded `JsonAsset` object assigns the wrong shape and the armature stays static.
- Setting `armatureName` before both assets are attached rebuilds against an incomplete factory and yields no armature; the armature key `uuid#atlasUUID` (`src/cocos/dragon-bones/DragonBonesAsset.ts:99-128`) only exists once the atlas asset has been parsed.
- A `playAnimation(name, 0)` call that finishes and holds is not a bug in the loop flag; pass `-1` (`src/cocos/dragon-bones/ArmatureDisplay.ts:1269`).
